claims.text: The local catalog and Bulbapedia unnumbered promo row identify row 222 as No.1 Trainer, a Neo Spring Road regional first place prize with no printed card number.
Bulbapedia gives the No.1 Trainer Japanese display name as Ｎｏ.１トレーナー and translation as No.1 Trainer.
Bulbapedia captions the Neo Spring Road print as illustrated by Ken Sugimori; Pokumon also lists Ken Sugimori for the Boy Neo Spring No.1 Trainer page.

Bulbapedia says the 2001 Neo Spring Road regional versions were awarded to champions from both Junior and Senior age divisions at regional Neo Spring Road tournaments held between February and March 2001.

Bulbapedia says these 2001 regional versions include the winner's name and regional conference, come in male and female variants, and are distinct from the Neo Spring Road Best in Japan final cards bearing the recipient's photograph.

Bulbapedia's No.1 Trainer page states that the Neo Spring Road print recognizes the Pokemon Card Game Official Tournament Battle Neo Spring Road champion, while the Neo Spring Road Best in Japan Deciding Match print recognizes the Battle Neo Spring Road Senior Tournament Best in Japan Deciding Match champion.

Bulbapedia trivia says the 2000-2002 regional No.1 Trainer print has six Pokemon in the illustration, while No.2 Trainer has four and No.3 Trainer has two; this visual rule is a useful rank check, not a substitute for physical authentication.

Bulbapedia's trivia discusses estimated early Japanese No.1 Trainer copy quantities and says an estimated 18 Neo Spring Road No.1 Trainer prints were awarded; Pokumon also lists estimated copies as 18. Treat this as collector/database estimate, not official copy-count truth.

No.1 Trainer row 222 matters because it turns a regional win into a personalized object: not just a card with Sugimori art, but a trophy that carries rank, age-division tournament structure, winner naming, regional conference, and the Neo Spring Road branch of organized-play history.

Agents should keep row 222 pinned to Neo Spring Road regional first place: No.1 Trainer / Ｎｏ.１トレーナー, Ken Sugimori, non-numbered unnumbered promo context, regional champion route, personalized winner-name/regional-conference treatment, and non-equivalence with Best in Japan photo cards, Neo Summer Road, No.2/No.3 Trainer ranks, 1997-1999 trophy prints, 2002 Battle Road prints, and later Worlds cards.
